findings.accepted_because: This standing minor compression slip (already accepted at synthesis-review iteration 2) stands in settled prose untouched in iteration 3; repairing it would disturb settled text on a tightly balanced concise layout while a reader who never learns that Bede transmitted Gregory on vv. 28-29 is not misled about Gregory's exposition of vv. 28-29 (already summarized at lines 11 and 19) or Bede's actual teaching on Luke 21:32-33.
findings.problem: At sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:21, compression of sections/04-lane-eschatological.tex:22 omitted the clause stating that St. Bede transmits St. Gregory's exposition of Luke 21:28-29 while retaining the opening scope phrase 'On vv.~28--29 and~32--33, St.~Bede (\work{In Lucae Evangelium Expositio}~VI) notes that \latin{Amen}...' ahead of a sentence whose content comes from v. 32 (followed by a separate sentence 'On verse~33...'). Consequently, vv. 28-29 (also listed in sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex:19 as 'on Luke~21:28--29, 32--33') receives no explicit exposition in the concise study.
findings.required_result: If sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:21 is reopened in a future edit, either add a brief clause noting that Bede transmits Gregory on vv. 28-29 before explaining Amen and generatio haec on v. 32, or narrow the lead-in to 'On verse~32' and trim '28--29,' from sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex:19.

findings.accepted_because: This compressed citation stands in settled prose outside REVIEW_SCOPE and mirrors upstream study-review accepted finding STU-012; repairing it would reopen settled synthesis prose without changing substance, and a reader is not misled about St. Leo's Advent teaching because bound Sermon 19.1 directly expounds Luke 21:34 against gluttony and worldly cares while bound Sermon 12.4 (already cited at line 44 and in References at 14:28) supplies the triad of prayer, fasting, and almsgiving.
findings.problem: Line 53 carries over the expansive study's compressed citation (sections/04-lane-eschatological.tex:30) attributing 'Advent fasting, prayer, and almsgiving to keep hearts from gluttony and worldly cares before that sudden Day' to St. Leo the Great's Sermon 19.1 alone. Direct verification of passage.nicene-and-post-nicene-fathers.series-2-volume-12.new-york-1895.leo-sermo-19.1 and leo-sermo-12.4 confirms that Sermon 19.1 expounds Luke 21:34 against surfeiting, drunkenness, gluttony, and worldly cares without naming prayer or almsgiving, while the tenth-month triad of prayer, fasting, and almsgiving stands in Sermon 12.4 (already cited at sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:44 and listed at sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex:28).
findings.required_result: If sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:53 is reopened in a future edit, cite both loci ('\work{Sermon}~19.1; cf.~\work{Sermon}~12.4') or narrow the clause to Sermon 19.1's own call to self-restraint against gluttony and worldly cares.

findings.problem: Both the scope note (line 6) and the Holy Scripture reference entry (line 16) refer to the secondary Douay-Rheims textual control as 'Gutenberg~1581' immediately beside 'Challoner 1899 American ed.'. Per edition.english-college-of-douay.douay-rheims-bible.challoner-gutenberg-1581 (edition.toml), '1581' is Project Gutenberg eBook number 1581 (released 1998 from Challoner's 1749-1752 revision), not a 1581 printing; placing 'Gutenberg 1581' beside '1899 American ed.' mirrors advisory STU-013 and risks reading like a publication year.
findings.required_result: In any future edit to sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex, expand 'Gutenberg~1581' at lines 6 and 16 to 'Project Gutenberg eBook~1581' so the catalog number cannot be mistaken for a printing year.

summary: Independent cold review of the concise study for the 1962 Roman Rite First Sunday of Advent (src/gemini/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/01-first-sunday-of-advent/synthesis.tex, sections/10-concise-inventory.tex through sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex, and generated/scriptural-date-location-page.tex) passes in source/HTML mode. Reading sections/10-14 alone before consulting the expansive study cleanly recovers all three interpretations' distinct governing questions, exegetical arguments, and four-sense distinctions across genuinely interleaved cross-proper comparisons (Luke 21:25-33, Ps. 84:8 & 13, Rom. 13:11-14a & Collect, Ps. 24:1-4, and altar prayers / threefold Advent). Subsequent comparison against the accepted expansive study (sections/01-09), manifests (publication.toml, proper-components.toml), and primary source loci under src/sources/ (Gregory Hom. 1 §§1-6, Bede Book VI on Luke 21:33, Ambrose Exp. in Luc. X.37-45, Cyril Sermon CXXXIX, Augustine De civ. Dei XX.14/16/24, Enarr. in Ps. 24.1-4 & 84.9/13-16, Sermo 185.1, Confessions VIII.12.29, Chrysostom Hom. 24, Bellarmine on Pss. 24, 79, 84, Bernard In Adventu 2, 3.3-4, 4.1, 5.1-3 & Missus est Hom. 1, Leo Sermons 12.4/17.1/19.1, Aquinas Postilla Ps. 24, Schuster pp. 321-323, Durandus VI.2-3, Beleth LV/LXIV, Rupert III.2, Sicard V.2, and Lapide on Rom. 13:11-14) confirms complete substantive alignment, preserved textual qualifications, plain-prose register, zero new source-dependent claims, zero leaked non-1962 medieval Gospels, and clean repair of the missing space after \dots at sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex:13 (the sole synthesis edit in REVIEW_SCOPE alongside the web-markup repairs in sections/01-06). Concrete passage-to-occurrence/place/date lookups on generated/scriptural-date-location-page.tex (orientation-v3 via research/chronology-table.tex and research/chronology-annotations.tex) succeeded cleanly: Gospel Luke 21:25-33 (rows 14-15) pairs Narrated event ('Jesus teaches in Jerusalem about the coming of the Son of Man' -> 'Date unresolved') distinctly beside Composition ('The Gospel of St Luke' -> 'Disputed: c. A.D. 70; Before Acts and the end of Paul's Roman imprisonment'); Introit Ps. 24:1-3, 4 (Vg.; Heb. 25, rows 1-3) pairs Traditional attribution ('David's reign in the usual chronology; Hebron, then Jerusalem' -> 'c. 1055-1015 B.C. (usual chronology; Corbett also reports dates 30-50 years later)') distinctly beside Historical setting ('Occasion date unresolved') and Composition ('Psalms' -> 'Before c. 165 B.C.'); and Epistle Rom. 13:11-14 (row 16) pairs Composition ('The Epistle to the Romans' -> 'Proposals span A.D. 57-58'), with explicit Vg./Heb. numbering key and pointer to the expansive study's full evidence notes. Limits: this is a source/HTML review and claims no rendered PDF pagination; two minor settled compression slips (SYN-006 on Bede vv. 28-29 and SYN-007 on Leo Sermon 19.1 mirroring upstream accepted STU-012) are recorded as accepted and one apparatus shorthand note (SYN-008 on 'Gutenberg 1581' mirroring STU-013) as advisory. Verdict: PASS.
